# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name

## Problem Statement

The new **Serial Seller** challenge (`ch-serial-seller`) must map to a persistent Steam achievement like the existing 12 challenges. The challenge-side mapping is added in the parent item (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J); this item covers the cross-repo pieces required before the parent can be reviewed.

## Users

- **Producers**: Need the Steam achievement registered on the Steamworks partner backend.
- **Developers**: Need the manifest entry to exist before the drift guard test will pass.
- **Players**: Need the Serial Seller achievement to appear in-game alongside the existing 12 achievements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.
3. The `core` submodule pointer in the main-street repo is bumped to the commit containing the manifest change.
4. The manifest drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) passes with the parent's mapping in place.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.

## Existing State

- 12 existing achievements in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, all with the pattern `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>`.
- The manifest is validated by `validateAchievementManifest()` and the drift guard test.
- Precedent: MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC (bumping core submodule pointer).

## Desired Change

- Add one entry to the manifest for the Serial Seller achievement.
- Commit to the core repo and bump the submodule pointer in main-street.
- Coordinate with the producer to register the achievement on Steamworks.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — Add `serial-seller` entry
- `core/` (git submodule) — Commit the manifest change
- `.gitmodules` / submodule index — Bump the submodule pointer

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J**: Sell 3 businesses challenge (parent, blocked by this item)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04**: Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (parent epic)
- **MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC**: Precedent for bumping core submodule pointer

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Steamworks backend delay**: If the producer has not yet registered the achievement on Steamworks, the achievement will not unlock for players even after code changes land. This is tracked as a separate action.
- **Scope creep**: Additional achievement metadata (e.g., icons, descriptions) may be desired later; record as a follow-up, not in scope for this item.
- **Submodule conflict**: Unlikely but possible if the core repo has concurrent changes; resolve by rebasing on latest core before bumping.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- This item was already sufficiently defined; no interview questions were asked. The description, scope, and acceptance criteria were clear and actionable.

## Dependency & audit resolution (2026-10-01)

Producer confirmed the Steamworks backend registration (AC2) is not yet done and requires a dependency chain. Two dependency items were created in the core project (CG store — the correct home for Steamworks backend work; worklog does not support cross-store dependency edges, so they are recorded here as cross-project references):

- **CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ** — Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine
- **CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1** — Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend *(depends on CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ)*

**AC2 therefore remains unmet until CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1 completes.** This item carries the `do-not-delegate` tag while externally blocked so the downtime worker does not re-dispatch it.

**Merge state:** the item's work is integrated into `dev`/`origin/dev` as commit `dd11ea4` (core → `d2d1f322`). The stale feature branch (which referenced the superseded core commit `4a287d4`) was reset to `dd11ea4`.

**AC4 call:** the drift guard requires the parent challenge-side mapping from **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J** (which depends on this item, so no cycle is possible). AC4 is verified at parent integration time; the mapping is present uncommitted in the working tree today and will pass permanently once the parent lands.

## Plan review — 2026-11-05 (verified state)

Verified against the current checkout: main-street `dev` at `f4f083ed`, `core` submodule pinned at `5a16c2fb`, superproject working tree clean.

- **AC1 met** — `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains `achievementId: serial-seller` with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false` (13 entries in total).
- **AC3 met** — the `core` pointer now pins `5a16c2fb`, later than the `d2d1f322` recorded above, and that commit contains the manifest entry.
- **AC4 preconditions satisfied** — the parent mapping (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J) is now **committed**, not uncommitted as stated above: `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps all 13 challenges, and the manifest and the game-side mapping agree exactly (13 ↔ 13, no drift in either direction). `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` is the guard that exercises this.
- **AC2 unmet / external** — unchanged: blocked on `CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1` (Steamworks backend registration). Not verifiable from the repository.
- **AC5** — no documentation change beyond the manifest entry was identified as required; the existing 12-achievement pattern is followed.
- **AC6** — enforced by the dev-push gate; not re-run by this planning session.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-05 — Plan re-run (effort Extra Small / Low, so decomposition skipped): six review stages run, AC coverage 100% (proceed), stage set to `plan_complete`. Recorded the verified AC state above; no child work items created.

# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI)

## Problem statement

The single-player End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) gives the
player a deliberate review-and-advance moment after each turn. Competitive
(human-vs-AI) play has no equivalent: after the shared day's closing
presentation (`presentCompetitiveClosing`) the day auto-advances with only the
transient per-seat income text (`Player 1: +X coins | Player 2: +Y coins`, via
`perSeatClosingSummary`) and the incident reveal. There is no moment to compare
each seat's standing for the round just completed — businesses owned, income
and expenses per seat. This item extends the End of Turn summary dialog to
competitive mode: one panel per completed round (one shared day where every
seat finished and the closing ran), with **owner-keyed rows** (businesses
owned, income/expenses per seat).

## Users

- **Main Street competitive player (human seat)** — plays week-by-week against
  AI seats on the shared street; after each shared day's animations finish,
  wants a persistent panel showing every seat's round result and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action (parity with the single-player dialog).

**User stories:**

- As a competitive player, when the shared day's closing animations finish, I
  see one panel summarising the round with a row per seat (businesses owned,
  income, expenses, net change, closing coins/reputation/score) so I can
  compare standings and learn from the round.
- As a competitive player, I click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next shared
  day — the day does not advance until I do.
- As a competitive player, I see the same (disabled) **[ Bank Loan ]**
  affordance as the single-player dialog, so the loans option is planned and
  consistent across modes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the single-player ledger; additions are optional and backwards-compatible — `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent.
3. The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours); **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.
4. Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the engine/headless close path; checkpoint save ordering (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged, and the dialog adds no save and mutates no state.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (Phaser-free model tests for owner-keyed rows, engine per-seat ledger tests, and a competitive-mode browser dialog test); **all related documentation is updated** (docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md competitive closing and end-of-turn summary sections, plus any README/dev references); **the full project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

# Intake brief: Remove broken `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` npm scripts from generated game repos

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** low · **Cross-repo:** yes (Tableau-Card-Engine core via the `./core` submodule) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL

## Problem statement

Every generated game repo (`tce-main-street`, `tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, …) declares two npm scripts — `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` — that point at `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, a file that does **not** exist in a game repo (Option C: game repos have no root `scripts/` tree; the scaffold lives in the core at `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`). Invoking either script fails with a module-not-found error. The working game-repo entry point, `npm run scaffold`, passes `--core-root ./core` and exists in every generated repo.

Root cause (resolved): `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` inherits the **entire** core `scripts` map from the core manifest (line ~280: `...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(manifest.scripts ?? {}))`). `core/package.json` legitimately declares `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` for core-repo use, so both leak unmodified into every generated game repo. The description's open "which is true" question is answered: the template **does** emit them, but only by inheritance — the fix is a template-side filter, not merely deleting two lines from each repo.

## Users

- **Game-repo maintainers (agents and humans)** — run npm scripts inside a game repo without tripping over dead entries.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of tce-main-street, I want `npm run scaffold:game` to either work or not be declared, so a script listed in my repo never fails with module-not-found."
- **Core scaffold owners (Tableau-Card-Engine)** — keep the template emitting only what a game repo can actually run.
  - *User story:* "As a core template owner, I want the scaffold to filter core-only scripts (including any future ones) out of generated repos, so a re-scaffold never reintroduces broken entries."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **This repo's `package.json` no longer declares `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games`.** `npm run scaffold` remains and resolves to `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street ...`. Guarded by a regression test (new `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts`) asserting the two broken keys are absent and every `scaffold*` script's target file exists.
2. **The scaffold template stops emitting them.** `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` filters the core-only `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` entries out of the inherited scripts map. Add a unit test in `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` whose manifest declares both keys and asserts the rendered `package.json` omits them, so a re-scaffold cannot reintroduce them (AC2 of the original item).
3. **The core change is delivered.** `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` + its test land in Tableau-Card-Engine (CG work item, per the MS↔CG pairing precedent of MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED↔CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q); this repo records the engine commit via its `./core` submodule pointer bump (`npm run engine:sync`), and `npm run scaffold` on a fixture checkout regenerates a `package.json` without the two keys.
4. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` documents `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo scaffold entry point and states that `scaffold:game(s)` are core-checkout-only commands; no game-repo-context doc references `scaffold:game(s)`. Core docs that use them (DEVELOPER.md, dev/creating-a-new-game.md, dev/multi-repo-architecture.md) are core-checkout context and remain accurate; a one-line "run from the core checkout" clarification is made where ambiguity exists.
5. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (changed-scope test gate plus the added regression tests; core-side suite green in the engine repo). The new `tests/tooling/` file is collected by the existing `unit` project (`tests/**/*.test.ts`, `vite.config.ts:222`) — no project-config change needed.

> **Traceability to the original ACs:** brief AC1 ← original AC1; brief AC2 + AC3 ← original AC2 ("resolve which is true first" resolved: the template emits them by inheritance, so a template filter is required); brief AC4 ← original AC3; brief AC5 ← original AC4.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo delivery** — the template fix lives in the Tableau-Card-Engine repo (`core/` submodule); this item cannot satisfy AC2 in-repo. Push policy applies to both repos: `dev` only.
- **No `npm run scaffold` against the live checkout** — re-scaffolding this repo today **drops 10 locally-added scripts** (`docs`, `docs:build`, `docs:preview`, `pretest`, `test:browser`, `generate:pack-assets`, `validate:storylines`, `storylines:graph:svg`, `docs:diagrams`, `balance:synergy-diversity-report`) because the template does not preserve repo-local extras. AC1 must be done with a hand edit; fixture-based re-scaffold verification lives in tests.
- **No CI beyond npm builds** — the npm build/test scripts are the verification vehicle.
- Implementation follows the mandatory worktree + build→test→commit order of the implement skill; work-item tracking via wl only.

## Existing state

- Issue type stays `chore`: the change removes dead config keys and adjusts the scaffold's config generation; it changes no runtime app behaviour (matches the `discovered-from` item's classification).

- `package.json` (this repo, lines 34–35): `"scaffold:game": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts"`, `"scaffold:games": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --all --core-root . --repos-dir .."`. Root `scripts/` contains only `run-tests.ts` and `soak-browser-waits.sh` — the target does not exist.
- `package.json` line 50: `"scaffold": "tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core"` — the working entry point (exists in all sibling repos too).
- `core/package.json` lines 31–32 declare the same two scripts **validly** (core has `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` `renderPackageJson` (lines ~274–312) inherits all core scripts, then overrides repo entry points; `scaffold:game(s)` pass through unchanged.
- 9 sibling game repos (`../tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-f5-verify`, `tce-fresh-verify`, `tce-repos-f9`) carry the same two broken lines — separate repositories, out of scope for this item's ACs (see Follow-ups).
- Related inherited-scripts bug of the same class: 8 more core-only entries arrive broken in every game repo (`test:smoke`, `test:dev`, `context:check`, `context:refresh`, `replay`, `transcripts:export`, `tf:generate`, `build:electron-main` — the last breaks `npm run package`/`package:win|linux|mac`). Excluded from scope (see Follow-ups).

## Desired change

1. Remove `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` from this repo's root `package.json` (hand edit; see Constraints).
2. In `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, filter the core-only keys out of the inherited scripts map — a small explicitly-named drop-list (or drop any inherited script that still references the core-only `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` target) with a comment explaining the Option C no-root-`scripts/` rationale and pointing at the follow-up item for the broader class.
3. Add/extend unit tests on both sides; bump the `./core` submodule pointer to the engine commit carrying the template fix.
4. Update `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (and the one-line core-doc clarification in Tableau-Card-Engine).

## Key Files

- `package.json` — remove the two `scaffold:game(s)` entries (this repo).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson`: drop core-only inherited scripts (template fix, engine repo).
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — extend MANIFEST fixture with `scaffold:game(s)` and assert they are omitted from the rendered `package.json`.
- `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts` (new) — regression guard: no `scaffold:game(s)` declared; every `scaffold*` script target exists.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — document `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo entry point; note `scaffold:game(s)` are core-only.
- `.gitmodules` / `gitlink core` — submodule pointer bump to the engine commit with the template fix.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Dead-key approach is undocumented assumption.** Assumption (recorded, not operator-confirmed): the fix is the narrow one from the item title — drop only `scaffold:game(s)`; the other 8 broken inherited scripts are a separate discovered follow-up (below). If the operator prefers the general filter (fixes all 10), AC1–AC5 grow; flagged, not blocking.
- **R2 — Submodule bump pulls unrelated engine commits.** The engine `dev` head is ahead of the pinned submodule (pinned `9ee194e0…` vs engine `dev` `1c9900a1…`). Mitigation: keep the bump to a reviewable commit; full suite must stay green (AC5).
- **R3 — Incomplete inheritance semantics.** Filtering only `scaffold:game(s)` is a stop-gap while the general class remains broken; over time more core-only scripts may be added. Mitigation: follow-up item tracks the general fix (`discovered-from` link).
- **R4 — Re-scaffold destructiveness discovered during intake.** If the template's preserve-on-re-scaffold behaviour is later expected to keep repo-local scripts, that is a separate enhancement — out of scope here.
- **Scope-creep guard:** sibling-repo clean-up, the 8-script general fix, and template local-script preservation are all recorded as follow-ups, not folded into this item.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** — "[test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe in generated vite.config.ts" (the `discovered-from` parent; same scaffold-template class of bug).
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED ↔ CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q** — engine-sync wiring precedent: core template change (in engine repo) + game-repo side + re-scaffold; the MS↔CG pairing model this item follows.
- **CG-0MVGF2QE9008NA5R** — version policy in `renderPackageJson` (the same function being changed).
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** — sibling-repo port of a core template guard; same cross-repo pattern.
- **CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA** — scaffold vite.config template ownership.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** – [test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe in generated vite.config.ts (open)
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** – Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version (completed)
- **MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O** – Engine dev tip renamed the story-line docs seam section (game doc-drift test pinned old heading) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mvcrgkzy007died, ac4, appear, banner, broken (+68 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: appear, banner, changes, context, core (+54 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, appear (+50 more)
> Assessment: `MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL` and `MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED` are genuinely related (same template/entry-point class). `MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O` matched on keyword noise (story-line docs seam) and is **not** relevant to this item; repo-file matches are incidental IDF matches. Full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0.md`.

## Follow-ups (recorded; out of scope)

- **Generalise the inherited-scripts filter** to all core-only entries that reference the absent game-repo `scripts/` tree (`test:smoke`, `test:dev`, `context:check`, `context:refresh`, `replay`, `transcripts:export`, `tf:generate`, `build:electron-main` — `build:electron-main` breakage disables `npm run package*` in every game repo). `discovered-from: MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0`.
- **Re-scaffold sibling game repos** (golf, blackjack, lost-cities, coloretto, feudalism, beleaguered-castle, f5/fresh-verify, repos-f9) or hand-remove the two lines; each is its own repo/worklog item.
- **Template preservation of repo-local scripts** on re-scaffold (R4).

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview was required: the seed context and acceptance criteria were sufficiently defined, and repository search resolved the description's open question ("resolve which is true first") directly:

- Q: Does `renderPackageJson` emit the two broken scripts, or were they hand-copied into game repos? — Answer (agent, repo search): It emits them **by inheritance** — `renderPackageJson` copies the core manifest's whole `scripts` map; `core/package.json` lines 31–32 are the source, and the rendered fixture (core test + node simulation) reproduces both keys. Source: `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (lines ~280–285), `core/package.json` (lines 31–32), `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (MANIFEST/inheritance assertions at lines 293–317), sibling repos `../tce-golf` etc. (same two lines at offset 21–22).
- Q: Can AC1 be satisfied by re-scaffolding this repo? — Answer (agent, simulation): No — re-scaffold would drop 10 locally-added scripts (`docs`, `pretest`, `test:browser`, `generate:pack-assets`, …); AC1 must be a hand edit. Source: node simulation of `renderPackageJson` over the live `core/package.json` vs current root `package.json` (listed in Constraints/Existing state).
- Q: Are the docs that mention `scaffold:game(s)` in game-repo context? — Answer (agent, repo search): No — all three sites (`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md:2075`, `core/docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md:119–123`, `core/docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md:271`) describe core-checkout invocation and stay accurate; they keep the core scripts' validity. # Competitive Turn Summary row end-to-end (tracer bullet)

## Goal

Competitive play gains the same review-and-advance moment single-player already
has: after the shared day's closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary
panel shows one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat, and the next shared
day starts only when the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**.

This is the tracer bullet slice: it cuts through **every** layer (engine ledger
→ Phaser-free model → overlay → scene gate) with the smallest useful row set
(businesses owned, per-phase income, net coin change), so the wire-up is
demonstrable end-to-end before later slices thicken the columns.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `TurnResult` gains an optional owner-keyed competitive round ledger (e.g. `playerRoundLedger?: OwnerRoundLedger[]`, or an optional per-owner field added to `OwnerIncomeResult`) exposing, per non-eliminated seat and in seat order: `businessesOwned`, the per-phase income subtotal, and `netCoinChange`. The field is optional and absent-safe: single-player, N=1 and headless callers are unchanged when it is absent.
2. `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` populates the ledger for N ≥ 2 (threaded through `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`, including the deferred dual-choice resume) without changing the coins deducted or credited, the shared phase order (Income → Incident → EndCheck), RNG consumption, or the emitted log lines.
3. `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` builds one owner-keyed competitive row per seat the closing surfaced, reusing `buildCompetitiveScoreboard` labels (`You` / `AI n`) and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours; it returns `null` when the result carries no competitive ledger, so single-player and browser callers are unaffected.
4. In the animations-enabled competitive closing path the panel appears after `presentCompetitiveClosing` completes, and `startTurnPhase` runs only on **[ Next Turn ]** — the next shared day does not advance before the click.
5. The panel renders **[ Next Turn ]** (primary, SFX via `safePlaySound`) and an always-disabled **[ Bank Loan ]** with the explanatory hint, behind an `onBankLoanAction` seam shaped so MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG can make it per-seat (`(seatId?: number) => void`) without re-plumbing. Reduced motion, replay and headless keep today's auto-advance pacing.
6. Parent criterion delivered — In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing. This slice delivers the businesses-owned, per-phase income and net-change columns; the ongoing-expense and closing-balance columns land in the dependent slices.
7. Parent criterion delivered — The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours); **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.

## Test-first checklist

Write these tests before the implementation edits (TDD within the slice):

- **Engine** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` — per-owner ledger values for a 2-seat and a 3-seat engine run; eliminated seat omitted; no ledger on N=1 / single-player; each seat's committed `PlayerRecord` coins identical to the ledger-less baseline.
- **Model** `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` — one row per seat, seat order, `You` / `AI n` labels and seat colours, per-row businesses owned / income / net; `null` when the competitive ledger is absent.
- **Gate** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-summary-gate.test.ts` — panel presented after the closing; `startTurnPhase` not called before **[ Next Turn ]** and called exactly once after; reduced-motion / replay / headless advance immediately.

## Minimal implementation

1. Declare the optional ledger types/fields in `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` (next to `TurnLedger` / `OwnerIncomeResult`) and re-export from `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts`.
2. Capture the values in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` where `playerIncome` is already produced, and carry them through `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`.
3. Add a competitive-row builder in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` (extend `buildTurnSummary` or add `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary`) using the scoreboard label/colour conventions.
4. Extend `showTurnSummaryDialog` (or add a thin competitive sibling sharing the same panel) in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` to render one row per owner, keeping the existing single-player call site working; delegate from `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`.
5. Gate the competitive tail in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (`presentCompetitiveDayTail`) with a `shouldGateCompetitiveTurnSummary` / `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate` pair mirroring the single-player gate in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
- `tests/main-street/helpers/turn-summary-dialog.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-summary-gate.test.ts`

## Reuse (do not rebuild)

- `buildCompetitiveScoreboard` / `resolveSeatColour` — the existing `You` / `AI n` labels and seat colour lookup, already reused by the Game Over model.
- The single-player panel, model and gate (`buildTurnSummary`, `showTurnSummaryDialog`, `shouldGateTurnSummary` / `presentTurnSummaryGate`) — extend, don't fork, so both modes share one presentation.
- `tests/main-street/helpers/turn-summary-dialog.ts` — the existing `[ Next Turn ]` finder/dismisser is reusable for the competitive browser test.

## Deliverables

- Optional owner-keyed competitive ledger on `TurnResult`, populated by the competitive closing.
- Competitive owner-row builder in the Phaser-free model.
- Turn Summary panel rendering one row per seat with **[ Next Turn ]** and a disabled **[ Bank Loan ]**.
- Competitive closing gate that blocks the next shared day until **[ Next Turn ]**.
- Engine, model and gate tests.

### Parent AC traceability

- **Parent AC 1** — "In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown) … The next shared day does not start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**. Reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog…" — delivered by AC1–AC5 here.
- **Parent AC 2** — "The dialog content is engine-computed and owner-keyed: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` … Additions are optional/backwards-compatible" — delivered by AC1–AC2 here (income, businesses owned, net change; expenses thickened in the sibling slice).
- **Parent AC 3** — "The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation … **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (disabled with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam …)" — delivered by AC3–AC5 here.

# Per-seat ongoing expense breakdown

## Goal

The competitive Turn Summary rows currently show income and net change but no
expense detail. Per-seat ongoing costs are computed today in
`applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` and thrown away (`void`, log-only). This slice
surfaces each owner's staff / community / business ongoing cost so the panel can
show what each seat actually spent in the round just completed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) returns a per-owner breakdown (`{ staff, community, business }`, signed zero-or-negative) instead of `void`; the coins deducted, the log lines, the iteration order and the insufficiency handling stay byte-identical for every existing caller.
2. The competitive round ledger carries that breakdown per seat (`ongoingCosts: { staff, community, business }`), while the single-player `TurnLedger.ongoingCosts` shape and semantics are untouched.
3. The Phaser-free model exposes per-owner expense rows (`staff` / `community` / `business` labels, signed values) plus a per-seat expenses total on each competitive row; single-player rows keep their existing shape.
4. The Turn Summary panel renders the per-seat expense rows and total for each competitive seat row, using the same labels and signed formatting as the single-player panel.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value at each layer (engine breakdown values incl. the Cost Cutter reduction and the sold-slot exclusion, model expense rows, panel rendering).
6. Parent criterion delivered — The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the single-player ledger; additions are optional and backwards-compatible — `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent. This slice delivers the per-seat ongoing-costs portion.

## Test-first checklist

- **Engine** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` — per-owner split for a mixed street (owned businesses + community spaces + staff), Cost Cutter reduction applied, sold slots excluded, and each seat's coins after the call identical to the pre-change baseline.
- **Model** `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` — expense rows and totals per seat, including a seat with zero expenses (all three rows present at 0).
- **Panel** competitive panel test — the expense rows appear in each seat's column.

## Minimal implementation

1. Change `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` to accumulate and return a `Map`/record keyed by owner id (staff salaries are already accumulated per owner; the community + business loop already keeps per-owner cost maps — return them instead of discarding).
2. Thread the returned breakdown into the competitive ledger produced by `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` (the same place `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` is called).
3. Add per-seat expense rows/total to the competitive row builder in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`.
4. Render the rows in the panel (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`), reusing the single-player label/format helpers.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` returning the per-owner expense breakdown.
- Per-seat expense breakdown on the competitive round ledger.
- Per-seat expense rows and totals in the model and panel.
- Engine, model and panel tests.

### Parent AC traceability

- **Parent AC 1** — the owner-keyed row must show "ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business)"; delivered by AC1–AC4 here.
- **Parent AC 2** — "the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs … on `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design)"; delivered by AC1–AC2 here.
- **Parent AC 5** — "At least one automated test per surfaced value (Phaser-free model tests for owner-keyed rows, engine per-seat ledger tests…)"; delivered by AC5 here.

# Per-seat net change, closing balances and incident/one-off parity

## Goal

Round out each competitive seat row with the figures single-player already shows:
net coin / reputation / score change for the day, the closing coin / reputation /
score balances, and that seat's share of the resolved incident and one-off
deltas — so a competitive player can compare standing properly, not just income.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The competitive round ledger carries, per seat: `netCoinChange`, `netRepChange`, `netScoreChange`, the seat's incident coin/reputation delta, and its one-off coin/reputation delta — all engine-computed, optional and absent-safe.
2. The identity `day-start snapshot + net == closing balance` holds per seat, and each seat's closing coins / reputation / score equals its committed `PlayerRecord` wallet after the closing (asserted against a real engine run, not hand-built fixtures).
3. The model exposes those values on each competitive row (net change, closing balances, incident and one-off deltas), and `null`/absent ledger data degrades to the existing row shape rather than throwing.
4. The panel renders per-seat net change and closing balances (coins / reputation / score) alongside the incident and one-off deltas, matching the single-player column ordering and signed formatting.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (engine reconciliation identity, model row values, panel rendering); single-player output is unchanged.

## Test-first checklist

- **Engine** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` — reconciliation identity per seat across two seeds; closing balances equal `PlayerRecord` wallets; an eliminated seat contributes no row.
- **Model** `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` — net and closing values per row; incident/one-off per row; absent optional deltas degrade gracefully.
- **Panel** competitive panel test — net change and closing balances rendered per seat.

## Minimal implementation

1. Extend the competitive ledger entry (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`) with the net, closing and incident/one-off fields.
2. Populate them where the competitive closing already knows the per-seat wallets and shared incident (`src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`; the per-owner incident routing already exists via `applyCompetitiveEventEffects`).
3. Expose the values on the competitive row builder in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`.
4. Render them in the panel (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`).

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Per-seat net / closing / incident / one-off figures on the competitive ledger.
- Model rows exposing and the panel rendering them.
- Engine reconciliation and model/panel tests.

### Parent AC traceability

- **Parent AC 1** — each owner-keyed row must show "net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score"; delivered by AC1–AC4 here.
- **Parent AC 2** — every value shown is "engine-computed and owner-keyed … testable without a browser and consistent with the single-player ledger"; delivered by AC1–AC2 and AC5 here.
- **Parent AC 5** — "At least one automated test per surfaced value"; delivered by AC5 here.

# Competitive summary invariants and edge cases

## Goal

Harden the competitive Turn Summary end-to-end: only the seats the closing
actually surfaced get rows, every non-competitive and non-interactive path keeps
today's pacing byte-for-byte, and the gate provably adds no save, no state
mutation and no RNG consumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Eliminated seats produce no row (no ghost rows): the panel renders exactly the seats the closing surfaced, and a test asserts row-count and row-identity against an engine run with one eliminated seat.
2. N = 1 and single-player closings never present the competitive panel; the existing single-player `shouldGateTurnSummary` behaviour (deferred only, skipping reduced motion / tutorial / replay / competitive) is unchanged and covered by its existing tests.
3. Headless, AI-driven and Monte-Carlo paths never invoke the panel and keep the `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS` bounded pacing; a test drives a headless competitive day to the next day without an overlay surface and asserts it advances.
4. The gate adds no checkpoint save and mutates no engine state or RNG: `presentCompetitiveDayTail`'s save-before-closing ordering is asserted (save called exactly once, before the closing presentation), and the engine state is deep-equal (ignoring presentation fields) before and after the gate resolves.
5. Never stalls: when the model build throws, the competitive ledger is absent, or the scene has no `showTurnSummaryDialog` / overlay manager, the next day starts immediately, matching the pre-gate pacing.
6. Parent criterion delivered — Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the engine/headless close path; checkpoint save ordering (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged, and the dialog adds no save and mutates no state.

## Test-first checklist

- **Gate** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-summary-gate.test.ts` — eliminated seat omission; N=1/single-player skip; headless advance; save ordering; missing-surface fallback; state immutability and no extra RNG draws.
- **Model** `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` — no row for an eliminated seat; graceful degradation when optional fields are absent.
- **Engine** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` — Monte-Carlo / headless competitive day unaffected (no ledger-dependent behaviour).
- **Browser** `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — existing browser flows that drive a competitive day end-to-end keep working once the panel is gated (dismiss via the shared helper where the subject is not the gate).

## Minimal implementation

1. Skip eliminated seats explicitly in the competitive row builder / ledger emission (the closing already filters `playerIncome`; make the row builder derive from the same filtered set and add the guard).
2. Add the mode guards to `shouldGateCompetitiveTurnSummary` (replay, reduced motion, no-owner / non-competitive state, game over) mirroring `shouldGateTurnSummary`.
3. Make `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate` fail-open: model throw, absent ledger or missing overlay surface → call `startTurnPhase` immediately.
4. Assert the save ordering and immutability in tests; fix any ordering drift found.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-summary-gate.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/helpers/turn-summary-dialog.ts`
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Eliminated-seat exclusion enforced and tested.
- Mode guards for the competitive gate.
- Fail-open behaviour verified.
- Save-ordering / immutability / headless-pacing tests.

### Parent AC traceability

- **Parent AC 1** — "one owner-keyed row per **non-eliminated** seat … Reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing"; delivered by AC1–AC3 and AC5 here.
- **Parent AC 4** — "Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in the scene presentation tail … Checkpoint save ordering … is unchanged; the dialog adds no save and mutates no state"; delivered by AC2 and AC4 here.
- **Parent AC 5** — "At least one automated test per surfaced value"; delivered by AC1–AC5 here.

# Colour of service businesses

## Problem statement

Service businesses render in a dark purple that is visually indistinguishable
from the flat purple face used by every upgrade card, so the two card families
read as the same thing at a glance on the street and in hand. At the same
time, an upgrade card carries no information about *what* it upgrades: all 39
upgrade cards share one uniform purple face regardless of the business they
apply to.

## Users

- **Main Street player** (primary) — scanning their hand and the market needs
  to distinguish a service business from an upgrade card instantly, and to see
  which family of business an upgrade belongs to without reading its title.
  - *As a player, I want service businesses in a colour no other card family
    uses, so I never mistake a service business for an upgrade card.*
  - *As a player, I want each upgrade card to show the colour of the business
    family it upgrades, so I can pick a relevant upgrade from my hand without
    reading every title.*

- **Colour-blind player** — the distinction must not rely on hue alone; the
  checkered pattern is itself a non-colour cue, and the upgrade card keeps its
  title and "for <Business>" target text.

## Existing state

- Synergy-type card faces are coloured from two parallel palettes:
  `CARD_FACE_PALETTE` (dark faces, `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`) and the
  bright `synergyColor` accent palette. The static Node generator
  (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) duplicates both; an
  existing test asserts the two copies of the face palette agree
  (MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4).
- Service currently holds dark purple `#6A1B9A` (face) / `0x9B59B6` (accent).
- Upgrade cards are flat purple: background `#6B4C9A`, accent `#9B59B6`,
  rendered by `generateUpgradeCardSvg` / `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and by
  `cardColorScheme` / the family branch in the `.mjs` generator.
- 39 upgrade rows in `src/card-data.csv` carry a `targetBusiness` name but no
  synergy column of their own; synergy must be resolved by looking the target
  name up among business **and** community-space rows (6 targets are community
  spaces: Community Garden, Health Kiosk, Library, Park, Playground, Town
  Fountain).
- 9 businesses are bridge cards with two synergy types; 11 upgrade rows target
  them (Cafe, Food Truck, Art Gallery, Day Spa, Flower Shop, Juice Bar, Yoga
  Studio, Teahouse).

## Desired change

1. **New service colour.** Replace Service's palette entries with a pink /
   magenta that no other synergy type uses, in **both** palettes (face and
   accent) and in **both** copies (TypeScript and the `.mjs` duplicate), so the
   palette-agreement test still passes.
2. **Checkered upgrade faces.** Upgrade card faces become a checkerboard of
   violet and the synergy colour of the business the upgrade targets, instead
   of the current flat purple.
3. **Bridge targets use both colours.** When the upgrade targets a card with
   two synergy types, the checkerboard uses both synergy colours (with violet
   in the remaining squares).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Service synergy type's face colour is a pink/magenta distinct from
      every other synergy colour, applied in `CARD_FACE_PALETTE`
      (`src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`) and its `.mjs` duplicate
      (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`); the existing
      TS/mjs palette-agreement test passes unchanged in intent.
- [ ] The bright Service accent colour (`synergyColor`) is updated to the
      matching pink/magenta family so icons, header tint and art backing stay
      consistent (the `expanded-card-pool` assertion is updated to the new
      value).
- [ ] A generated upgrade card face renders as a checkerboard of violet and
      the target's synergy colour, for both the runtime generator
      (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` / `generateUpgradeCardSvg`) and the static
      `.mjs` generator, with both paths producing the same pattern.
- [ ] An upgrade targeting a single-synergy business yields a two-colour
      checkerboard (violet + that synergy colour).
- [ ] An upgrade targeting a bridge business (two synergy types) yields all
      three colours: violet plus **both** synergy colours.
- [ ] An upgrade whose target synergy cannot be resolved (unknown or missing
      target) degrades safely to the existing flat purple face and never
      throws.
- [ ] Upgrade cards remain legible: title, "for <Business>" target text, cost
      badge and art stay readable over the checkerboard (existing contrast
      expectations in the SVG tests are preserved).
- [ ] New unit tests cover: the new service colour, single-synergy
      checkerboard, bridge-target three-colour checkerboard, unresolvable
      target fallback, and TS/mjs pattern agreement.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The static Node generator runs outside the TS build and cannot import
  TypeScript modules, so any palette or resolver change must be duplicated
  there and kept in agreement (existing project pattern).
- Upgrade synergy colour must be **derived**, not added as a new CSV column:
  `targetBusiness` is the only link today, and adding data columns would
  invalidate CSV checksums and pack fixtures.
- Upgrade **card** faces change only. The in-game board upgrade accent (the
  gold corner shard on an upgraded business, `UpgradeOverlaySpec`) and the
  owner-coloured seat border are out of scope — they are a separate visual
  language and were deliberately settled by MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF.
- Card faces must remain readable at the reduced hand/stacked scale (the art
  zone and text column must not be masked by the pattern).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts` — new Service entry in `synergyColor` and

# Engine DEVELOPER.md lists reduced motion among the paths that omit deferResourceApplication

Discovered from: MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X (Turn summary dialog suppressed by reduced motion setting).

## Problem

`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (the Tableau-Card-Engine submodule), section *Deferred End-of-Turn Mutation* → bullet *Deferred `processEndOfTurn`*, says:

> Tutorial, reduced-motion and replay paths omit the flag (legacy immediate behaviour, no regression — AC5).

After MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X the reduced-motion path does **not** omit the flag: the scene (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `endTurn`) takes the deferred closing path under reduced motion, so the Turn Summary dialog has a `requiresDeferredClosing` result to gate on. Only the tutorial and replay paths still omit it.

## Why it was not fixed in the MS session

- `core` is a git submodule (a separate repository, detached HEAD at the engine pin `5a16c2f`). A working-tree edit leaves the submodule dirty, and `npm run build` runs `engine:sync` (non-soft), which **refuses** to sync a dirty submodule ("never clobber") — every later build in this repo would fail.
- A local commit inside the submodule is discarded by the next `engine:sync` (it checks out the remote target), so the fix would silently vanish.
- The engine checkout has no worklog (`wl` there reports "not initialized"), and pushing to the engine repo's `dev` is not authorised from a game-repo session.

## Fix

In the Tableau-Card-Engine repository, amend that bullet so only the tutorial and replay paths are named as flag-omitting, and state that the reduced-motion path takes the deferred closing so a game's Turn Summary gate can present its summary dialog (cross-reference the game-side behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` no longer claims the reduced-motion path omits `deferResourceApplication`.
2. The bullet names the tutorial and replay paths as the immediate/flag-omitting ones and explains why the reduced-motion path is deferred.
3. No code change is required; the engine's documentation guards (if any) still pass.

# Intake Brief — Gate specialization-skill effects by staff type (MS-0MW3LTMHT001PRDT)

## Problem statement

Specialization skills are assigned from a global 16-skill pool regardless of a staff card's type, and the street-wide folds aggregate every employed member's skills. As a result, a **business-staff** member can hold a **management-company-scope** skill (Cost Cutter, Negotiator, Brand Ambassador, the four incident-mitigation skills, the Town Gossip baseline) and leak a player/street-scope effect, while a **management-company** member can draw **business-scope** skills (Chef, DJ, Networker, …) that can never resolve. The shipped behaviour therefore contradicts the two-type model reconciled in `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` (and GDD D.4.8), where a skill takes effect only from a member whose type matches the skill's scope.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — needs specialization skills to be a meaningful, type-consistent hiring signal: a business-staff hire improves its business, a management-company hire improves the player's turn, never an unexplained cross-scope leak.
- **Game designer / balance owner** — needs the shipped behaviour to match the documented two-type model so balance tuning and the skill catalog are trustworthy.
- **Implementing developer** — needs a deterministic, testable gate that preserves seeded reproducibility and existing save compatibility.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a skill held by a business-staff member to affect only that business, so that hiring decisions match the two-type model.
- As a game designer, I want assignment to draw skills consistent with a staff card's type, so that no card can hold an effect it can never realise.
- As a developer, I want the seeded assignment stream to stay deterministic, so that same seed ⇒ same game is preserved.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Scope gate (behavioural).** A business-staff member holding a management-company-scope skill (Cost Cutter, Negotiator, Brand Ambassador, any of the four incident-mitigation skills, or the Town Gossip baseline) produces **no** player- or street-scope effect; equally, a management-company member holding a business-scope skill produces **no** per-business buff. The Operations Manager salary discount remains a business-staff effect applied to its employing member.
2. **Type-consistent assignment (deterministic).** Business staff draw only business-scope skills; management-company staff draw only player-scope skills plus the Town Gossip baseline. The stacking caps (≤1 income-boost, ≤1 reputation-boost beyond baseline) remain per-member and type-neutral.
3. **Determinism preserved.** The assignment stream stays seeded and reproducible (same seed ⇒ same assignments); existing determinism tests continue to pass, and new determinism tests cover the type-consistent draw.
4. **Documentation updated.** `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` records that the follow-up gap is closed (or removes the follow-up section), and the GDD D.4.8 / `card-catalog.md` cross-references stay consistent. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **Validation.** At least one automated test proves the scope gate (both leak directions) and the type-consistent assignment; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Preserve determinism.** The assignment RNG stays the dedicated `createSeededRng(numericSeed ^ 0x5eed)` stream; do not perturb the main RNG stream (deck shuffles, market draws, challenges).
- **Preserve save compatibility.** Skills persist as stable id arrays; the staff type is derived from `employedAtSlot` and must not require a new stored field.
- **No new skills or magnitude changes.** The 16-skill catalog and its magnitudes are unchanged; this item only gates effects and constrains assignment.
- **Two staff types only.** Business staff = has `employedAtSlot`; management-company staff = no `employedAtSlot` (GDD D.4.2/D.4.8). No third type or skill flag.
- **Documentation-only gap closure.** Update the follow-up section of `specialization-skills.md` to mark the gap closed; do not re-open the two-type design.
- **UK English** throughout.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — `STAFF_SKILL_CATALOG` (16 skills, 4 categories); `assignSkillsToApplicant(rng)` draws from the **global** pool and always adds the Town Gossip baseline; `assignStaffApplicantSkills(state)` seeds assignments across the staff deck and market row. The catalog carries no scope/type field today.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `getEmployedSpecializationSkills(state)` flattens **every** employed member's skills (street-wide); `getEmployedSpecializationSkillsForBusiness(state, slot)` flattens only that slot's members; `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs`, `computeIncidentSkillBuffs`, `computeStreetOngoingCostReductionPct`, `computeRefreshCostDiscount`, `computeStaffSalaryDiscount`, `computeReputationGainMultiplier`, etc. translate skills to effects.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — consume the street-wide and per-business aggregations.
- `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` — § *Shipped cross-type assignments — reconciliation follow-up* documents the two gaps and states they are not yet fixed; the skill table already classifies 8 business-staff and 8 management-company skills.
- Existing tests: `staff-skill-assignment.test.ts`, `staff-skill-assignment-state.test.ts` (determinism, stacking, baseline), `staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts`, `staff-effect-scoping.test.ts`, `specialization-skills-two-types.test.ts` (doc contract).

## Desired change

1. **Scope gate.** Make street-wide/player-scope effect folds read only management-company members' skills, and per-business folds read only business-scope skills from the employing business's members — so a skill is inert when its scope does not match its holder's type. Keep the Operations Manager salary discount as a business-staff effect.
2. **Type-consistent assignment.** Draw business-scope skills for business staff and player-scope skills for management-company staff, always keeping the Town Gossip baseline on management-company cards. Preserve the per-member stacking caps and the seeded, reproducible stream.
3. **Docs + tests.** Update the `specialization-skills.md` follow-up section (gap closed/removed) and GDD/card-catalog cross-references; add determinism and scope-gate tests.

- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — scope-gated `getEmployedSpecializationSkills` / `getEmployedSpecializationSkillsForBusiness`; per-business fold gating.

- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4.8) / `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — cross-reference consistency.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — determinism regression:** changing the candidate pool per type alters the seeded stream; *mitigation:* dedicated tests assert same-seed reproducibility across both types, and the salt/main-stream separation is preserved.
- **Risk — partial gate:** gating only the assignment leaves a stale save or hand-built fixture with a cross-type skill leaking; *mitigation:* the scope gate is enforced at the aggregation site, not only at assignment, and tests cover a cross-type skill held by both staff types.

# Loan payoff dialog: carry the payoff across a paused closing

discovered-from:MS-0MW3SN58E009HC84

## Goal (user story)

As a player whose loan retires in a turn that also pauses on an event-choice
dialog (or a bankruptcy bailout offer), I want to still see the debt-free
congratulation once the pause resolves, so that no payoff goes unnotified.

## Context

`MS-0MW3SN58E009HC84` presents the payoff dialog in the closing presentation
slot (`MainStreetLoanPayoffModel.presentLoanPayoffDialogs`), after the closing
animations and ahead of the End of Turn summary. Two pauses resolve **after**
that slot, so their payoffs are currently never presented:

- **Event choice**: `processEndOfTurn` retires the loan and then pauses
  (`choicePending`) before `finishTurnPresentation` reaches the presentation
  slot. The resume path (`onEventChoice` → `finishDeferredEndOfTurn`) builds a
  fresh result that does **not** carry `loanPayoffs`.
- **Bankruptcy bailout**: the deferred result pauses on the loan offer
  (`pendingLoanOffer`); `onLoanOfferChoice` resumes through
  `completeDeferredClosingTail`, which never presents payoffs. A declined offer
  ends the run, so game over correctly wins there; an **accepted** offer
  continues the run with no congratulation.

The paused path never duplicates a dialog (there is only one presentation slot),
so this is a *missed* notification, not a duplicate.

## Desired change

Carry the paused closing's `loanPayoffs` into the resumed flow (the same
pattern `pendingBankingHint` uses for the banking hint) and present them via
the existing `presentLoanPayoffDialogs` sequencer on the continuing resume
path — never on a resume that ends the run (game over wins).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An event-choice-paused closing that retired a loan presents exactly one
   congratulation when the choice resolves, and never two.
2. A bailout-paused closing where the seat accepts an offer (the run continues)
   presents exactly one congratulation; a declined offer (the run ends)
   presents the game-over overlay and no congratulation.
3. The dialog still appears only after the closing presentation and never
   alongside another modal.
4. Unit tests cover both pause paths, including the no-duplicate rule.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — carry the payoffs across
  `presentEventChoiceDialog` / `presentLoanOfferDialog` and present them on the
  continuing resume.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanPayoffModel.ts` — `presentLoanPayoffDialogs`
  (reused unchanged).
- `tests/main-street/loan-payoff-turn-flow.test.ts` — the pause/resume cases.

## Constraints

- Presentation only: no engine, arithmetic, wallet or RNG change.
- One modal at a time; the summary/bailout/event-choice pacing is unchanged.
